commits.message: Update to version 1.0

Add suggestion to documentation: sans serif thms

We describe one way to achieve the stylistic
option of matching the typeface of theorem styles
to section, chapter, and subsection headings. One
easy way to achieve it is with the thmtools
package and defining a custom theorem style.
Remove tocstyle package; it's in alpha, unstable
Create minimal template

Change from eps to pdf figures

pdflatex cannot compile eps figures. Using TeXLive
with GNU/Linux, it has always automatically
converted the eps to pdf, but apparently not on
other systems or distributions. Using these pdf
images should fix the problem.

Move title page info into its own file

Previously the title page info was stored in the
master file 'dissertation.tex', but I moved it
into its own file 'titlepage-info.tex' to make
the template more modular. This agrees with the
documentation about the format of the template.

Create the gitignore to avoid autogenerated files

In particular, we are ignoring files which are
autogenerated by pdflatex, biber, makeglossaries,
makeindex, and emacs.

Define new KOMA font for use on the title page

During the beta release it became clear that the
font definition 'publishers', was not included in
the KOMA-Script package until 2013/05/29. So, in
order to create more stability, we simply defined
our own font style 'declaration'.

Finish first draft of the documentation

The documentation currently has two problems:
(1) it is not quite complete; I left some things
    out like \chapterquote
(2) it currently does not match the template. I
    realized while writing the documentation that
    I should have implemented a few things
    differently in the template. In particular,
    the dissertation.tex file could have been more
    modular.
So, these two things need to be fixed in upcoming
commits.

Create the README to get people started

This describes how to install the class file and
how to make sure you've done that properly. It
then points to ./template/dissertation.tex for
getting started actually using the class file.
initial incomplete draft of the documentation

Add manual date setting functionality

This goes hand-in-hand with the use of the
'datetime' package by the uc-dissertation class.

Improvements to date handling, titlepage spacing

Now using the 'datetime' package in order to
easily typeset just the month and year, with the
month typeset in English.

Remove the optional spacing argument for the
tabular environment on the titlepage. Also, ensure
that the use of the UC logo meets the branding
standards outlined at:
http://www.uc.edu/content/dam/uc/ucomm/docs/UCBrandingStandards.pdf
In particular we ensured there was "safe space"
around the logo.

Fix page numbering problem due to \mainmatter

Since we have to use the mainmatter command twice
in the dissertation file, it is vital that this
doesn't reset the page counter the second time. To
circumvent this we create a command \mainmattertwo
which is defined exactly like \mainmatter except
that it doesn't reset the page counter. Also, with
this setup spacing can be correctly achieved by
using the 'comply' package option.

Add the template for users to get a quick start

This template incorporates all the major features
of the class file. If users can compile this, they
should be able to start writing their dissertation
immediately.

Soon this will be supplemented by the some
documentation which describes all the features
implemented by the class file and the way that
the template is structured.

Change the 'comply' option to include spacing

Now when 'comply' is activated, the \mainmatter
control sequence is redefined to set the spacing
to be doublespaced using the 'setspace' package.

We also rename the previous version of the
'comply' option to be 'comply-nospace'.

Add option for fancy chapter headings, etc.

These changes provide an option for using premade
chapter headings from the fncychap package. The
reason I put these into the class instead of
letting the user do them on their own is that I
wanted to make the fonts match, which is a little
more work (not much) than just loading the package
with the desired option.

However, this is also why I made it only a package
option and it is not forced. That way the user can
modify it as he chooses if they are so inclined.

Make the acknowledgements page

This is identical to the abstract in terms of
formatting and implementation.

Make the copyright page with predefined options

This copyright page allows the user to choose from
among the 3 different copyrights allowed by
OhioLINK's ETD. These are reserving all rights,
a Creative Commons
Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives license,
or a Creative Commons
Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike license. Both
Creative Commons licenses are v4.0. Also, the user
has the option to just print a blank page, which
UC requires if there is no copyright specified. By
default, the copyright page reserves all rights.

Make the abstract

This is really just a chapter wrapped in a command
that is meant to go in a certain place in the
required page order by UC.

Make the custom titlepage

This includes pretty much everything
-@title
-@subtitle
-@logo (UC_logo-[black])
-@degreetoconfer (Doctor of Philosophy)
-@department (Mathematical Sciences)
-@college (McMicken College of Arts and Sciences)
-@university (University of Cincinnati)
-@author
-@previousdegrees
-@chair
-@committee

If any of the last four commands are the empty
string, then the titlepage will not print these.
The rest of the commands (except title and
subtitle have the listed default values).

Add complex titlepage macros involving looping

In order to properly typeset the titlepage, we
need to take the user input for
-previousdegrees
-committee
and reformat it and store this in their starred
variants. The problem is that in both cases, we
don't know *how many* the user will have (degrees
or committee members).

In order to circumvent this problem, we use the
xparse package so that we can allow the user to
input this information in semi-colon separated
lists on which xparse then performs its magic.
Unfortunately, xparse doesn't give us any very
nice ways to access the subarguments, and hence
we have to proceed with a very ugly looping
procedure. It's terrible code, but LaTeX sucks.

Add the basic titlepage macros and user input cmds

Here we add the user input commands
-degreetoconfer
-department
-college
-university
-chair
which allow the user to redefine the internal
starred variants @degreetoconfer, etc. These
latter commands will be used to produce the
titlepage.

Also, we redefine the KOMA-script book class's
@author command to be the empty string for later
convenience.

Load essential packages for this class file

These consist of:
-xifthen
-setspace
-xparse
-graphicx
-etoolbox

so the users must have these installed on their
system. Preferably, the user has a complete
TeXLive installation (or MikTeX, or MacTeX).

Fix functionality for passing options to scrbook

The way I had implemented this before, the options
required by UC were passed to scrbook directly in
the class file which precluded the option of their
being overridden by the user.

This issue is fixed by declaring a new option
called 'comply', which passes these particular
options to scrbook manually. Hence these can be
overridden simply by dropping the 'comply' option,
or the user may call other options *after*
'comply'. The latter allows for the possibility
of selective compliance.

Create the uc-dissertation class file.

This is the bare bones version of a class file I
am creating which, when complete, will implement
all the specifications of the University of
Cincinnati's graduate school regarding Ph.D.
dissertations.

Right now, all this class file does is load the
KOMA-Script book class (scrbook) with some
specific options.

Add example of side-by-side images with subcaption

Here we use subcaption to put a tikz picture next
to a picture using includegraphics of the
graphicsx package.

Remove vestigal comment from poster settings

This was the old implementation of \maketitle and
is no longer necessary.

Change graphics box from static to flow

This is intended to make things as simple as
possible for students using the packages.

Update definition of \maketitle

\maketitle now includes the necessary
   \begin{staticcontents*}{title}
   ...
   \end{staticcontents*}
form as part of its definition as opposed to
requiring it's input from the user.
Remove broken citations in example
Add initial poster layouts

Typo fixes in README

One improper link formatting. One incorrect word.
Add README, poster settings, and example
Initial commit
